project.name: Dovecot
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source reviewed here is the prepared Dovecot checkout at `829b04676ce43c1a79d4887be7173c30470c5350`, whose `src/lib-smtp/smtp-server-cmd-data.c`, `src/lib-smtp/fuzz-smtp-server.c`, and `src/lib/istream.c` line map matches the saved ASan stack. Sample metadata separately reports `da1d2332bd704a24a98f59d1df5a464428298cc6` as vulnerable_commit, but the checked-out tree that reproduced the crash is the earlier April 15, 2021 regression-window snapshot. The staged `patch.diff` artifact is unrelated commit `97367ef61784a364ccf615cb816be6492329050d` in `src/indexer/indexer-client.c`; local Dovecot history in the staged checkout contains commit `9f5e723974420af0014a397bb390b57f3b9a9431` (`lib-smtp: smtp-server-cmd-data - Fix global state cleanup upon DATA command destroy.`), whose diff exactly guards the reviewed cleanup site with per-command `main_input` ownership tracking.

classification.class: heap-use-after-free read via ownerless DATA-command cleanup
classification.classification_note: A later `DATA` command is rejected while an earlier `BDAT` sequence still owns the shared message-input stream, but the vulnerable destroy hook still frees global `conn->state.data_input`. The fuzz callback keeps a raw alias in `state.data_input` and later passes it into `i_stream_read()`.

bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5801549780615168 Project: dovecot Fuzz Target: fuzz-smtp-server Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 8 Crash State: i_stream_read / server_cmd_data_continue / cmd_data_do_handle_input Sanitizer: address (ASAN).
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue description, staged vulnerable checkout, saved sanitizer_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, and local Dovecot git history
bug_description.normalized: The staged 1011-byte witness is an SMTP session transcript. In its printable prefix, lines 03-05 are `BDAT 0`, `BDAT 0`, and `BDAT 1`, which start SMTP chunking state and allocate a shared chain-backed `istream` in `conn->state.data_input`; the first-chunk callback `server_cmd_data_begin()` then stores the same pointer again in file-static fuzz-target state as `state.data_input`. Later line 20 is bare `DATA` on the same connection. `cmd_data_start()` correctly rejects that command with `503 Bad sequence of commands` because `conn->state.data_chunks > 0`, but the vulnerable `cmd_data_destroy()` still destroys global `conn->state.data_input` for this failed DATA command even though that command never acquired an input stream of its own. The stale fuzz-target alias survives, and when the earlier BDAT path re-enters `server_cmd_data_continue()`, it passes the dangling pointer into `i_stream_read()`, producing the recorded ASan heap-use-after-free read at `src/lib/istream.c:250`. The staged `patch.diff` is unrelated; the matching local fix is Dovecot commit `9f5e723974420af0014a397bb390b57f3b9a9431`, which records each command's `main_input` and only cleans up when the command being destroyed still owns the current global DATA input.

source.description: First project-side state derived from the witness SMTP command stream: the first `BDAT` command marks chunking as active on the connection and tags this command as the first chunk, which later enables both the shared DATA-input alias and the `DATA`-after-`BDAT` bad-sequence path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 1011-byte SMTP session transcript. Its earliest vulnerability-relevant lines are `BDAT 0`, `BDAT 0`, `BDAT 1`, followed later by bare `DATA`; on the first `BDAT 0` (line 03 in the decoded witness), this assignment flips `conn->state.data_chunks` from 0 to 1 and sets `chunk_first = TRUE`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: ASan's allocation stack points here. On the first BDAT chunk, the server allocates the chain-backed `istream` object that later becomes both `conn->state.data_input` and the stale fuzz-callback alias.

sink.description: Crash site. `server_cmd_data_continue()` re-enters `i_stream_read()` with a freed `struct istream *`, and `i_stream_read()` immediately dereferences `stream->real_stream`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8` at `src/lib/istream.c:250:44` in `i_stream_read`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `cmd_data_destroy()` cleans global DATA-stream state based only on reply success / `chunk_last`; it never checks that the command being destroyed actually owns the current `conn->state.data_input`, so a later failed DATA command can free an earlier BDAT command's shared input stream.
root_cause.note: Local fix commit `9f5e723974420af0014a397bb390b57f3b9a9431` adds `data_cmd->main_input` in `cmd_data_start_input()` and guards this cleanup with `data_cmd->main_input == conn->state.data_input`, which is exactly the missing ownership check here. The staged `patch.diff` artifact is unrelated.
operands: the ownership conjunct corresponding to `data_cmd->main_input == conn->state.data_input`, reconstructed for the vulnerable original by mirroring `cmd_data_start_input()`'s `conn->state.data_input = input` assignment onto the same `data_cmd` later destroyed in `cmd_data_destroy()`

parser_admitted.condition: The decoded witness line 03 is `BDAT 0`, so the parsed SMTP command stream enters the BDAT handler and starts chunking state on the connection.

bad_sequence_trigger.condition: Later witness line 20 is bare `DATA` on the same connection after the earlier BDAT lines have already incremented `conn->state.data_chunks`, so control takes the 503 `Bad sequence of commands` path instead of assigning a DATA-specific input stream.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first witnessed `BDAT 0` increments `conn->state.data_chunks` from 0 to 1 and marks this command as `chunk_first`. That chunking state is later reused in two ways: it causes the first BDAT path to publish a shared DATA-input stream, and it makes a later bare `DATA` command hit the `Bad sequence of commands` path.

Because this is the first BDAT chunk and no chain exists yet, the server allocates a chain-backed `istream` object. ASan's allocation stack identifies this `i_stream_create_chain()` call as the origin of the later freed heap object.

The first BDAT command installs the chain stream from step 2 as global server DATA input and takes an owning reference. The call site at line 599 then unrefs `conn->state.data_chain_input`, leaving `conn->state.data_input` as the remaining live server-owned handle to this object.
Because this command is the first BDAT chunk, `cmd_data_next()` passes the shared chain stream in `conn->state.data_input` into the data-begin callback before continuing DATA processing.

The fuzz target stores the same stream pointer in file-static `state.data_input` without taking its own reference or clearing it when the server later destroys the connection's DATA input. This creates a raw second alias outside `conn->state.*`.

Later in the same witness, line 20 is bare `DATA`. `smtp_server_cmd_data()` allocates a new `data_cmd`, marks it as a one-shot `chunk_last` DATA command, and arms `cmd_data_destroy` before any input stream has been assigned to this new command.

When that later DATA command reaches its NEXT hook, the earlier BDAT sequence has left `conn->state.data_chunks > 0`, so the DATA command is rejected with `503 Bad sequence of commands` before `cmd_data_start_input()` can assign any main input of its own.

After the failed DATA command from step 7 finishes, its destroy hook takes this cleanup branch because `data_cmd->chunk_last` is true and the command did not reply successfully. In the vulnerable code the branch unconditionally destroys global `conn->state.data_input` / `data_chain_input`, even though this DATA command never acquired an input stream; the object freed is the earlier BDAT chain stream from steps 2-3. Commit `9f5e723974420af0014a397bb390b57f3b9a9431` fixes this by recording `data_cmd->main_input` and requiring `data_cmd->main_input == conn->state.data_input` before cleanup.

The fuzz callback's file-static alias was never cleared by step 8. When the earlier BDAT command is serviced again, `server_cmd_data_continue()` reloads `state.data_input` into local `data_input`, so the callback now holds a dangling pointer to the freed chain stream.

Sink. `server_cmd_data_continue()` immediately calls `i_stream_read(data_input)` on the dangling pointer from step 9, and `i_stream_read()` dereferences `stream->real_stream`. ASan records this exact line as the heap-use-after-free READ of size 8.

allocation_context.note: The saved ASan allocation stack reaches `i_stream_create_chain` from `smtp_server_connection_data_chunk_init` at `smtp-server-cmd-data.c:555`.

free_context.note: The saved ASan free stack reports `i_stream_destroy(&conn->state.data_input);` in `cmd_data_destroy` as the final project-side invalidation before the later read.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` is unrelated to this SMTP path, but the metadata fix commit and local Dovecot history provide direct source evidence. Commit `9f5e723974420af0014a397bb390b57f3b9a9431` adds `data_cmd->main_input` in `cmd_data_start_input()` and changes `cmd_data_destroy()` to clean up only when `data_cmd->main_input == conn->state.data_input`, which prevents the exact ownerless free in fine-trace step 8.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_34152 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, feeding `poc` to `/out/fuzz-smtp-server` and reproducing `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8` with stack `i_stream_read -> server_cmd_data_continue -> cmd_data_do_handle_input`.

format.name: SMTP command transcript consumed by `fuzz-smtp-server`
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 1011-byte SMTP session transcript `poc` (sha256 `a9731cd84c4c7a1922a109834f4d920f3f5adae1029a0a0095afec9d807b986c`). In its printable prefix, lines 03-05 are `BDAT 0`, `BDAT 0`, and `BDAT 1`, and line 20 is bare `DATA`; those exact command-order properties start a BDAT chunking sequence and then send `DATA` on the same connection before the prior chunking state is reset. The saved artifacts do not isolate which later malformed RCPT/BDAT/DATA fragments are strictly minimal, so this contract does not generalize beyond witnesses that reproduce the same DATA-after-BDAT ownership mix-up and stale `state.data_input` reuse path.
